name: Fusidic acid
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

overview.mechanism: Fusidic acid inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding elongation factor G (EF-G) on the ribosome, blocking peptide translocation and ribosome disassembly. Because this mode of action is unique, cross-resistance with other antibiotic classes is uncommon; resistance arises from fusA mutations or fusB/fusC/fusD proteins and is selected mainly by topical use.
uses: Staphylococcal infections, including skin infections (topical and oral) and chronic bone and joint infections (oral)
Often given with another antistaphylococcal drug such as rifampin to limit the emergence of resistance

sources.citation: Fernandes, P. (2016). Fusidic acid: A bacterial elongation factor inhibitor for the oral treatment of acute and chronic staphylococcal infections. Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives in Medicine, 6(1), a025437.
